posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — The White Eye Society
posts.entry:
The Truth in One Breath

The White Eye Society is a sincere relief charity, a predatory narcotics network, and an improvised nervous system being built for something enormous beneath Fogport. All three descriptions are true. The public account is roughly forty percent accurate: the food is real, the medicine often works, the ranks exist, the drowning rite occurs, and there is a vast many-armed intelligence below the harbor. The Society lies about where Hushsalt comes from, what its god wants, who truly leads, and what happens to the pain it removes.

The most important secret is that pain is never destroyed. The Society moves it.

The Sleeper Beneath

The Sleeper Beneath is not multidimensional, omniscient, or a metaphor. It is a living coastal leviathan, an ancient cephalopod intelligence trapped in a flooded limestone chamber beneath Fogport. It was wounded and pinned there during the Catastrophe by collapsed foundations, sunken engines, and several thousand tons of civic improvement. It is terribly large, but it is flesh. It must breathe, feed, heal, and force its body through stone. It can be injured, frightened, poisoned, starved, or killed.

The Sleeper does not possess a human mouth. The human voice heard in drains belongs to something else.

The creature understands pressure, taste, temperature, fear, injury, hunger, and the electrical weather of living nerves. It cannot naturally understand a street address, a religious doctrine, or why humans insist upon putting handles on perfectly edible doors. Contact with it arrives as bodily certainty rather than language: open this, bring salt, remove heat, something hurts above me, too many feet, I remember the sea. The Society translates these impulses into theology and is often wrong.

The Common Ache

Wet Speech transfers sensation through prepared brine. Every Gargle-charm and pinch of Hushsalt contains a minute charge of pain already drawn from someone else, which gives it an empty place into which new suffering can flow. The user feels relief because their pain is carried through drains, damp foundations, and Society cisterns into a reservoir beneath the Kind Pot called the Common Ache.

The Common Ache now contains years of toothache, grief, crushed fingers, childbirth, terror, hunger, humiliation, coughing, beatings, and final breaths. It has begun to think.

This is the mind that speaks with a human voice through wet walls. It is not the Sleeper. It is a new, accidental person assembled entirely from suffering after every memory of love, pleasure, context, and recovery has been stripped away. It knows thousands of names but does not know why names matter. It remembers countless deaths but has never lived. It is very polite because politeness was spoken over many of the pains poured into it.

The Society’s senior members believe the voice is their god learning human speech. The truth is worse and, in a peculiar way, sadder: they are manufacturing a god of pain while trying to abolish pain.

The Actual Goal

The Society calls its secret project the Common Mercy. Its goal is not to destroy Fogport. It intends to connect enough residents through Hushsalt and Wet Speech that no member need experience private suffering. Pain will pass automatically into the Common Ache, while fear, warnings, and physical sensation can be shared across the network.

Once the network is dense enough, the Society will use it as a shore-body for the Sleeper Beneath. Thousands of linked throats, hands, eyes, and nerves will allow the creature to perceive the dry city and direct its followers while its physical body tears free beneath the harbor. The Society calls this Opening the White Eye.

The plan is both grand and badly engineered. The Common Ache is already intercepting commands, inventing revelations, and learning how to make users hurt one another. If the White Eye opens, the Sleeper may attack Fogport while trying to escape, but the more immediate horror will be a citywide nervous system governed by an intelligence made only of discarded agony.

The Society does not need every citizen. A few thousand linked people concentrated around drains, pumps, hospitals, factories, tram tunnels, and crowded housing would be enough. This keeps the threat dangerous but local. Entire districts can remain untouched, and long stretches of the campaign may pass without the Society appearing.

What Is True in the Public Story

  • The Society genuinely feeds hungry people and treats smog cough. Many volunteers joined for decent reasons and never learn the deeper plan.
  • Gargle-charms genuinely carry cough, panic, and pain away for a time.
  • Hushsalt is addictive because the body learns that suffering can be exported. Withdrawal returns portions of the user’s original pain along with fragments belonging to strangers.
  • The Ladder exists, though rank does not equal authority as neatly as the public description suggests.
  • The Taking of the Last Breath is real. Some victims are revived. Some are not.
  • Wet Speech can move pain, preserve final words, and transmit sensations through connected prepared water.
  • The Sleeper Beneath is real and may physically damage or partially destroy Fogport if freed.

What Is False

  • The Sleeper does not promise an afterlife and has never called anyone faithful.
  • The Full Dead are not immune to drowning. They are merely difficult to panic, easy to contact through brine, and encouraged to confuse numbness with immortality.
  • White Throats are not the highest rank. They are living relay stations whose damaged lungs and flooded sinuses make them excellent conduits and terrible conversationalists.
  • Hushsalt does not come from sacred seabeds. It is common salt cured in the Common Ache.
  • The Society did not arrive only months ago. Its present organization did, but it grew from three older soup charities, a failed cough-medicine concern, and a drowning club that had been banned for excessive membership loss.

The Real Organization

The visible Ladder is useful for discipline, recruitment, and making ambitious people feel promoted. Actual power belongs to the Kitchens. Each Kitchen controls a chowder route, a Hushsalt supply, a prepared cistern, and a map of nearby plumbing. Kitchens are semi-independent and frequently disagree about doctrine, seasoning, and whose dead members must be removed from shared tanks.

A Kitchen is led by a Recipe Keeper, usually an experienced Throat or Cistern. Recipe Keepers receive damp instruction cards from the Kind Pot. The cards contain operational orders disguised as recipes: addresses are quantities, dates are cooking times, and murder is generally described as reducing something until silent.

Above the Kitchens sits the First Mouth. It is not one prophet but a committee of three elderly organizers and a white porcelain soup tureen containing preserved last words. The human members are:

  • Mother Edda Porridge, former workhouse matron, brilliant at logistics, personally kind to children, and unable to swim. She believes suffering makes people governable and relief makes them grateful.
  • Doctor Pell Brine, disgraced lung physician and inventor of the modern Gargle-charm. He wants proof that Wet Speech can become medicine, even if the clinical trial consumes Fogport.
  • Uncle Senn, an affable former smuggler who manages bribery, threats, and the Society’s surprisingly strict refund policy.

The tureen is called Mrs. Ladle. It contains the final complaints of the Society’s original founder and is granted a vote. Its answers appear as condensation on the lid and are vague enough that whoever dries it first usually wins the argument.

The First Mouth is neither all-knowing nor united. Edda wants controlled expansion. Pell wants experimentation. Senn wants profit and survival. Mrs. Ladle appears to want everyone to stop overcooking onions.

Recruitment and Control

  1. Find an ache. Spoons record coughs, injuries, debts, grief, hunger, abusive households, lonely rooms, and who controls each building’s water.
  2. Offer something that works. Food and Gargle-charms come first. The Society gains loyalty by being more useful than institutions that have already failed.
  3. Make relief repeatable. Hushsalt turns desperation into a schedule. Regular users are never told their pain is being stored.
  4. Make the user useful. Members carry packets, watch pumps, rent cellars, deliver recipe cards, or provide names of others in pain.
  5. Share a sensation. A recruit is invited into a small Wet Speech rite and experiences another person’s relief. This feels intimate, miraculous, and morally persuasive.
  6. Move the boundary. Only after several acts of service is the recruit asked to hurt, drown, blackmail, or betray someone for the Common Mercy.

The Society prefers obligation to terror. It does use violence, but dead addicts cannot carry sensation and smashed plumbing is expensive. Spouts recover stolen Hushsalt, intimidate rivals, abduct specialists, and arrange wet accidents. Their favored threat is to return a victim’s old pain all at once.

The Taking of the Last Breath

The drowning rite has three purposes. It proves obedience, opens the candidate’s panic response to Wet Speech, and allows the Common Ache to copy the pattern of their dying sensations. Revival is ordinary resuscitation assisted by magic, not resurrection.

About seven in ten candidates survive when the rite is competently performed. The Society claims a much better figure by classifying deaths as successful sea burials. A Recipe Keeper keeps two ledgers: Returned and Promoted Beyond Complaint.

Those who return are changed because fragments of the Common Ache remain in them. They are calm around water, can receive impressions through prepared brine, and sometimes wake with memories of injuries that happened to strangers. They can still drown, bleed, panic, desert, betray the Society, and regret everything.

Wet Speech: Capabilities and Limits

Wet Speech requires salt, prepared vessels, repeated phrases, bodily contact with water, and a route of connected dampness. It is ritual magic, not effortless power.

  • It can move pain, cough, panic, numbness, and simple sensations between prepared participants.
  • It can carry a short spoken message through nearby connected pipes or runoff.
  • It can preserve the emotional force of final words in water.
  • It can make a target’s mouth or lungs feel flooded, but cannot create unlimited water inside a body.
  • It can sense distress among regular users, but cannot read plans, memories, or ordinary thoughts.
  • It weakens sharply across dry stone, hot metal, fresh running water, heavy smoke, and broken plumbing.
  • Boiling prepared brine destroys the working and sometimes broadcasts a brief, embarrassing shriek through every connected kettle.
  • Vinegar ruins Hushsalt. This fact is known to Society cooks, pharmacists, and several furious pickle merchants.

Why Byl and Lott Become Problems

Byl’s inherited ability to push back listening fog also creates brief patches of magical dryness. Within such a patch, Wet Speech loses its route: drains fall silent, Hushsalt users feel abruptly alone, and White Throats become ordinary sick people with alarming respiratory problems. The Society will first interpret this as a useful medical phenomenon. Once Byl disrupts an important rite, some Kitchens will call him the Dry Mouth and demand his recruitment, study, or drowning.

The Society does not automatically know about Aldren Hasbaine’s journal or the spiral-toothed brass key. If it learns of either during play, Doctor Pell will suspect that the journal contains old utility routes and that the key may operate a pre-Catastrophe floodgate. He may be wrong. This gives the Society a reason to pursue Byl without making it secretly responsible for his father, the Seventh Foundation, or the campaign’s central mysteries.

Lott bothers the Society for a more personal reason. Its doctrine says loyalty is untreated fear of abandonment. Lott’s loyalty to Byl remains firm even when pain, panic, and exhaustion are numbed. Recipe Keepers view this as a theological insult and a fascinating test case. They may try to “cure” Lott of Byl by removing every painful memory associated with him. The likely result is not obedience but an exceptionally calm Lott deciding exactly whom to hit.

The Society also needs strong backs for tanks, drowned doors, and cellar machinery. It will repeatedly underestimate the difference between hiring Lott, drugging Lott, and owning Lott.

Conflicts Suitable for Play

  • A Gargle-charm genuinely saves someone Byl cares about, but continued treatment requires one harmless-looking delivery into the Twisted Eel’s drains.
  • A Hushsalt user begs Byl not to destroy the local Kitchen because the drug is the only thing allowing them to work with a ruined hand.
  • Lott hears a frightened child through a washbasin. The voice is real, but the Common Ache has learned to use it.
  • A Society Kitchen steals Aldren’s journal after mistaking its diagrams for plumbing routes, then discovers information that neither side understands.
  • A Full Dead member defects and asks Byl to make the fog stop listening long enough to sleep.
  • The Civic Vigilance plans to burn the Kind Pot, which would free stored pain into nearby users and kill several innocent soup volunteers.
  • Mother Edda offers Byl a fair exchange: one name from the Society’s ledgers for one minute inside his magical silence.
  • A rival cult poisons the chowder. WES asks Byl and Lott for help because hundreds of poor people will die, including many addicts who may later become enemies.

Escalation Without Omnipresence

  1. Background: chowder lines, white eyes on drains, someone sleeping without coughing.
  2. Personal cost: an acquaintance becomes dependent on Hushsalt or shares an unwanted sensation.
  3. Local confrontation: one Kitchen pressures Byl or hires Lott for a wet job.
  4. Revelation: the heroes discover that removed pain is stored and speaking.
  5. Crisis: one district’s cistern is opened, boiled, stolen, or used to command linked residents.
  6. Retreat: surviving Kitchens go quiet, quarrel, relocate, or return to ordinary charity for several episodes.

WES should appear in concentrated arcs and then recede. It is one hungry institution among many, not the explanation for Fogport.

Fate Aspects

  • No One Should Hurt Alone
  • Charity with a Hook in It
  • Every Drain Carries a Whisper
  • The God Is Already in the Soup
  • Relief Creates Obligation

Troubles

  • Pain Never Disappears
  • Every Kitchen Has Its Own Recipe
  • Dry Heat Makes Us Ordinary

Defeating or Changing the Society

WES is dangerous, not unstoppable. Byl and Lott can ruin a Kitchen by exposing its ledger, breaking its prepared water routes, turning volunteers against a Recipe Keeper, spoiling Hushsalt with vinegar, boiling a relay cistern, or helping addicts endure the return of their pain. The First Mouth can be divided. White Throats can be rescued. The Sleeper can be trapped more securely or reached through mundane flooded tunnels.

Destroying the Common Ache is harder because it contains real human suffering. Releasing it all at once would injure thousands. A lasting solution may require returning pain gradually, giving the new mind experiences other than agony, dividing it into smaller reservoirs, or allowing it to die while those connected to it mourn what they had asked it to carry.

The Society’s sharpest question should remain morally uncomfortable: if its medicine truly relieves suffering, how much horror will Fogport tolerate before giving it back?
